topic: model efficiency; compression and dynamic inference
status: bounded cross-paper design lead; hardware-aware evaluation is established, global novelty unverified
claim: In this six-paper cell, several efficiency claims are expressed as parameter count, binary code length, or FLOP budgets, while the target concern is often physical inference latency/energy. Those quantities are related but not interchangeable. The actionable next test is a matched hardware-specific quality–latency–energy–memory Pareto comparison, not a claim that earlier work ignored hardware altogether.
positive_evidence: ATQ evaluates binary-retrieval mAP against code bits and sampled data sizes, not deployment energy or device latency.

SMH's central results compare accuracy with trainable-variable budgets; its structured mapping is argued to avoid material latency overhead, but the study is not a cross-device energy/latency benchmark.
Shallow-Deep Networks constrain per-sample FLOPs and tune confidence thresholds on a small unlabeled holdout; attached heads increase parameter/storage requirements.
The historical survey distinguishes compression/speed metrics and calls hardware-aware design important, underscoring that model size alone is not a universal runtime measure.
counterevidence: Hardware-aware efficiency research already exists: SqueezeNext reports accelerator-simulated speed/energy, and MultiTASC reports mobile/server device latency and SLO outcomes.
SMH deliberately structures hashing to improve memory locality and reports low latency overhead; early-exit methods directly target per-sample inference cost.
Parameter/operation counts remain useful portable proxies when hardware is not specified; they are not invalid, only insufficient for every deployment claim.

falsifiable_test: Reimplement one representative hashing/compression, early-exit, and static compact-model baseline under the same training data and quality target. On at least two mobile CPUs and one edge GPU, measure batch-1 and batched p50/p95 end-to-end latency, joules/inference, peak resident memory, serialized bytes, and FLOPs/parameters. Include warmup, repeated runs, clock/power details, confidence intervals, and both in-distribution and shifted accuracy. The design lead weakens if rankings by parameters/FLOPs predict latency/energy Pareto order across devices and workload regimes.
limitations: The sampled methods target retrieval, image classification, or parameter compression and use different datasets; this is a measurement-design synthesis, not a pooled effect or a claim that these specific papers make false claims.

status: bounded observed interaction; not a universal ranking claim
claim: The sampled evidence does not support a single cross-task model-efficiency winner: ATQ’s relative retrieval ranking changes between CIFAR-10 and MNIST; SMH reports parameter/accuracy behavior that is more consistent within ResNets than across EfficientNet/MobileNet families; and early-exit quality at fixed FLOP budgets varies by task and architecture. A fair comparison should predefine the target task, model family, and resource budget and report interaction effects.
positive_evidence: ATQ/CQ generally perform strongly on CIFAR-10, while Spectral Hashing often leads on MNIST; the paper also notes sample-count fluctuations.
SMH finds ResNet models compressed to the same parameter count have similar accuracy, but this pattern does not hold as clearly across EfficientNet and MobileNet variants.
Shallow-Deep Networks show different early-exit accuracy/savings across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny ImageNet, and multiple CNNs.
counterevidence: Each paper’s method has legitimate in-scope wins: ATQ is competitive for CIFAR retrieval, SMH compresses several families, and SDN can cut compute while maintaining accuracy in evaluated image tasks.
Only a few datasets/families are included here; cross-paper outcome definitions are not comparable and no universal interaction estimate follows.

falsifiable_test: Run paired comparisons over predeclared datasets and architectures at equal serialized model size, training-compute budget, and target-device latency/energy. Report performance by task and family with repeated seeds and confidence intervals; test method×dataset and method×architecture interactions. The interaction lead weakens if rankings remain stable after controlling budget and uncertainty across independent task families.
limitations: Findings come from heterogeneous 2016–2019 studies and a small fixed cell, not a meta-analysis; the comparisons motivate controlled replications only.

topic: early-exit inference; confidence calibration and distribution shift
status: bounded evaluation lead; broad early-exit novelty rejected
claim: The sampled SDN study tunes confidence exits on a small unlabeled holdout and reports FLOP/accuracy tradeoffs on three in-distribution image datasets, but does not test distribution shift. Confidence gating can therefore be treated as a workload-conditional control policy, not a universal accuracy-preserving guarantee. This limitation is already an active research area, so the remaining question is whether calibrated exit policies retain their quality–compute frontier under realistic shifts and hardware constraints.
positive_evidence: SDN reports practical confidence-based exits, but results vary across CIFAR-10/100 and Tiny ImageNet and thresholds are chosen on an unlabeled holdout.
A separate 2019 benchmark shows uncertainty/calibration behavior can deteriorate under dataset shift, making shift evaluation relevant to confidence-gated systems.
A 2025/2026 confidence-gated training paper is direct evidence that early-exit training and inference alignment remains actively studied.
counterevidence: SDN demonstrates substantial in-scope compute savings and sometimes accuracy equal to or above the original CNN; difficult examples are often routed deeper.
Confidence-gated training reports benefits on Indian Pines and Fashion-MNIST; early-exit research is not absent.
Dataset-shift calibration evidence does not by itself prove that SDN’s exits fail under shift; a direct paired evaluation is required.

sources.title: Confidence-gated training for efficient early-exit neural networks

falsifiable_test: Compare fixed-threshold, validation-calibrated, and confidence-gated early-exit models on clean and predeclared corruption/domain shifts. At matched p95 latency and joules/inference, report top-1 risk, calibration error, selective risk, and exit-depth distribution with repeated seeds. The lead weakens if calibrated quality and resource frontiers remain stable under shifts and on held-out hardware.
limitations: The sampled early-exit paper is an older CNN image study. Shift evidence and newer confidence-gated evidence are follow-ups with different models/tasks; no direct SDN shift test was performed in this batch.
